# GRC Management Metrics

**Six ratios, computed from the repository, never hand-quoted.**

**Owner:** MLRO · Compliance Engineering (operational)
**Source of truth:** [`data/grc-metrics.json`](../../data/grc-metrics.json) — generated by [`scripts/grc-metrics.mjs`](../../scripts/grc-metrics.mjs)
**Enforcement:** `node scripts/grc-metrics.mjs --check` (CI + `npm test`) and [`test/grc-metrics.test.mjs`](../../test/grc-metrics.test.mjs)
**Review cadence:** read at the monthly management review and the quarterly board pack; the snapshot itself refreshes with the change that moves it.

> **Why generated.** A hand-maintained metric is stale the day after it is
> written — that is exactly how the readiness review came to claim "37 workflows"
> against an estate of 46. Every number here is derived from a committed
> artefact, and CI fails if the snapshot drifts from the live repository. A
> figure in a board pack can be traced to the commit that produced it.

---

## 1. Current values

| Metric | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Control Effectiveness Rate** | **100%** (61/61) | Assurance-matrix §1 rows whose named proof artefacts all exist ÷ rows with an automated proof |
| **Compliance Completion Rate** | **33.3%** (6/18) | Obligations at *met* ÷ regulatory obligations. 10 partial, 2 pending |
| **KRI Breach Rate** | **12.5%** (1/8) | Instrumented KRIs in breach ÷ instrumented KRIs |
| **Overdue Issue Rate** | *not instrumented* | Open items carry an owner and a closing condition but no target date |
| **Third-Party Assessment Coverage** | **71.4%** (5/7) | Vendors with a settled safeguard/DPA position ÷ vendors in the register |
| **Audit Finding Closure Rate** | **95.2%** (20/21) | CAPA rows at *Closed* ÷ all CAPA rows |

Regenerate after any change to the assurance matrix, the obligation register,
the third-party register or the CAPA log:

```
node scripts/grc-metrics.mjs           # print
node scripts/grc-metrics.mjs --write   # refresh the snapshot
```

## 2. How to read the two low numbers

**Compliance completion at 33.3% is not a control failure.** *Met* is reserved
for obligations that are built, operating and evidenced end to end. Ten of the
eighteen regulatory obligations sit at *partial*: the control exists and is
evidenced, and a human act — a board sitting, a counsel confirmation, a training
delivery, an audit round — is outstanding. Each names the
[open-actions](open-actions-register.md) item that closes it. The metric tracks
the same reality as that register, in one number: the engineering is done, the
human acts are not.

**Third-party coverage at 71.4%** is the two outstanding vendor confirmations —
the Asana DPA on file and Anthropic's counsel transfer-basis — which are
open-actions items 2 and 5. It is the one KRI currently in breach (KRI-04).

**Audit finding closure at 95.2%** is HA-08: the transaction-monitoring engine
is built and its feed connection is a firm decision (item 6). One open finding
with a named owner is a healthy log, not a backlog.

## 3. Why one metric is null

Overdue Issue Rate needs a target date to age against, and open items do not
carry one — they carry an owner and a condition that closes them. Rather than
invent deadlines or quietly report 0%, the metric reports **null with its
reason**, and the corresponding KRI-09 stays in the appetite register marked
*not instrumented*. Instrumenting it is a board act: setting target dates on the
open-actions register.

An uninstrumented KRI is excluded from the KRI-breach denominator — never scored
as passing. CI enforces that distinction.

## 4. Counters behind the KRIs

| Counter | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `modelToolDeclarations` | 0 | No model call declares tools — RA-03 holds |
| `governanceDriftCount` | 0 | No prompt fingerprint or agent-capability mismatch — RA-05 holds |
| `unjustifiedSuppressions` | 0 | Every OSV suppression carries a written reason |
| `obligationsWithoutOwner` | 0 | No orphaned obligation |
| `obligationsWithoutWatchSource` | 1 | ISO/IEC 42001 — a standards body, not a supervisor feed. Tolerated at ≤ 1 |
| `openActionsWithoutTargetDate` | 17 | Every open action carries an owner and a closing condition; **none carries a deadline**. This is the missing input behind KRI-09 (§3) — it counts rows in the [open-actions register](open-actions-register.md) whose `Target date` cell holds no ISO date. With no such column, every row counts. Setting the dates is a board act (item 17) |

## 5. What CI enforces

- **Freshness** — `--check` compares the snapshot against a live recomputation;
  a stale board figure fails the build rather than reaching a board pack.
- **Basis** — every metric must state its denominator definition. A number
  without one is a claim, not a metric.
- **KRI wiring** — every KRI in [`risk-appetite-statement-2026.md`](risk-appetite-statement-2026.md)
  must key on a metric the script actually computes, with a threshold the
  evaluator understands; an uninstrumented KRI must say why.
- **No timestamps** — the snapshot carries none, so identical repository state
  always produces an identical file and the check never cries wolf.

## 6. Framework mapping

| Framework | Clause | How this satisfies it |
|---|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 42001 | 9.1 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation) | Defined metrics with defined methods, computed on every build |
| NIST AI RMF | MEASURE 1.1, 2.1 | Metrics tied to risks, with limitations stated rather than hidden |
| COSO ERM | Principle 16 (assesses substantial change) | Drift in the estate moves the number, and the number is checked |
| GRC practice | Essential management metrics | Five of the six computed; the sixth reported null with its reason |
